'''Glen Robert Van Brummelen''' (born May 20, 1965) is a [[Canadians|Canadian]] historian of mathematics specializing in the [[history of trigonometry]] and historical applications of mathematics to [[astronomy]].

He is president of the [[Canadian Society for History and Philosophy of Mathematics]],<ref>[http://www.cshpm.org/contact/council.php CSHPM Council] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131227134824/http://www.cshpm.org/contact/council.php |date=2013-12-27 }}, retrieved 2013-12-26.</ref> and was a co-editor of ''Mathematics and the Historian's Craft: The Kenneth O. May Lectures'' (Springer, 2005).

He has been involved in the summer program [[Mathpath]] since 2004 and is the creator of "Glensheep" and their evolution. <ref>[https://www.mathpath.org/about/facultystaff/faculty MathPath Faculty and Staff]</ref>

== Life ==
Van Brummelen earned his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] degree from [[Simon Fraser University]] in 1993,<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=15656}}</ref> and served as a professor of mathematics at [[Bennington College]] from 1999 to 2006. He then transferred to [[Quest University Canada]] as a founding faculty member. In 2020, he became the dean of the Faculty of Natural and Applied Sciences at [[Trinity Western University]] in [[Langley, British Columbia (district municipality)|Langley, BC]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.twu.ca/news-events/news/trinity-western-university-welcomes-new-dean-faculty-natural-and-applied-sciences|title=Trinity Western University Welcomes New Dean of the Faculty of Natural and Applied Sciences |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=29 May 2020 |website=Trinity Western University |access-date= 24 November 2024}}</ref>

Glen Van Brummelen has published the first major history in English of the origins and early development of trigonometry, ''The Mathematics of the Heavens and the Earth: The Early History of Trigonometry''.<ref>McRae, Alan S. (2009), Review of ''The Mathematics of the Heavens and the Earth'', {{MR|2473955}}.</ref> His second book, ''Heavenly Mathematics: The Forgotten Art of Spherical Trigonometry'', concerns [[spherical trigonometry]].<ref>{{citation|title=A forgotten discipline (review of ''Heavenly Mathematics'')|journal=Metascience|doi=10.1007/s11016-013-9836-9|first=John M.|last=Steele|date=July 2013|s2cid=254793113 }}</ref><ref>Funk, Martin (2013), Review of ''Heavenly Mathematics'', {{MR|3012466}}.</ref>

In 2016 he received a [[Deborah and Franklin Haimo Awards for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics|Deborah and Franklin Haimo Award for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics]].<ref name=web>{{Cite web|url=https://maa.org/member-communities/maa-awards/teaching-awards/section-award|title=Recipients of the Deborah and Franklin Tepper Haimo Award for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics; Mathematical Association of America|website=www.maa.org|access-date=2024-10-07|archive-date=2024-06-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240608175318/https://maa.org/member-communities/maa-awards/teaching-awards/section-award|url-status=dead}}</ref>

As of 2026 he is on sabbatical<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Glen R. Van Brummelen, PhD {{!}} Trinity Western University |url=https://www.twu.ca/profile/glen-van-brummelen |access-date=2026-09-09 |website=www.twu.ca |language=en}}</ref> as an Erskine Fellow at the [[University of Canterbury]] in Christchurch, New Zealand.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-06-05 |title=Honour Roll 2025 {{!}} UC |url=https://www.canterbury.ac.nz/about-uc/what-we-do/teaching/erskine-programme/honour-roll-and-visitor-profiles/by-year/honor-roll-2026 |archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20260608134256/https://www.canterbury.ac.nz/about-uc/what-we-do/teaching/erskine-programme/honour-roll-and-visitor-profiles/by-year/honor-roll-2026 |archive-date=2026-06-08 |access-date=2026-09-09 |website=www.canterbury.ac.nz |language=en}}</ref> He was previously awarded the [[Erskine Fellowship]] in 2010, 2017 and 2019.<ref name=":0" />

==Works==
*''The Mathematics of the Heavens and the Earth: The Early History of Trigonometry'' Princeton; Oxford: Princeton University Press, 2009. {{ISBN|9780691129730}}, {{OCLC|750691811}}
*''Heavenly Mathematics: The Forgotten Art of Spherical Trigonometry'' Princeton; Oxford: Princeton University Press, 2013. {{ISBN|9780691175997}}, {{OCLC|988234342}}
*Trigonometry: A Very Short Introduction; Oxford: Princeton University Press, 2020 {{ISBN|9780198814313}}, {{OCLC|1101269106}}
*''The Doctrine of Triangles: The History of Modern Trigonometry'' Princeton; Oxford: Princeton University Press, 2021 {{ISBN|978-0691179414}}, {{OCLC|1201300540}}
